steps: Divine determinative AN (𒀭) marks the name as theistic
Syllabic signs A (𒀀) and NU (𒉡) spell Akkadian /Anu/
Anu is the Sumerian/Babylonian sky-god and head of the divine assembly
Sumerogram EN.LÍL (𒂗𒆤), 'lord of the wind/air'
Divine determinative 𒀭 is often prefixed in theocratic contexts
Akkadian scholarly tradition renders the long /ī/ with a macron
Akkadian E-a is written É (𒂍, 'house') + A (𒀀)
The divine determinative 𒀭 marks the theonym
Sumerian counterpart Enki is written EN.KI (𒂗𒆠)
sources: Black & Green, Gods, Demons and Symbols of Ancient Mesopotamia

steps: The Inanna sign (𒈹) is a ligature used for the goddess of Uruk
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
Akkadian Ištar is a related but distinct theonym
Syllabic signs IŠ (𒀹) and TAR (𒁯) spell Akkadian Ištar
Divine determinative 𒀭 marks the goddess
The name is etymologically linked to Sumerian Inanna
Sumerogram AMAR.UTU (𒀫𒌅), 'calf of the sun'
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
Later Babylonian orthography uses syllabic Mar-duk
The Nabû sign (𒀝) functions as a logogram for the god of writing
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
The macron in Nabû marks long /û/
sources: Black & Green, Gods, Demons and Symbols of Ancient Mesopotamia

steps: Logographic spelling of the underworld god
Divine determinative 𒀭 marks the theonym
Akkadian Nergal lord of the underworld city Kutha
Syllabic spelling TI.AMAT (𒋾𒊩𒆳)
Divine determinative 𒀭 marks the primordial goddess
The long /ā/ is marked with a macron in scholarly transliteration
The sun-sign UTU (𒌓) serves as logogram for the sun-god
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
Akkadian Šamaš continues Sumerian Utu
sources: Black & Green, Gods, Demons and Symbols of Ancient Mesopotamia

steps: The number 30 (𒌍) is the logogram for the moon-god
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
Sumerian Nanna / Akkadian Sîn
Syllabic spelling AŠ-ŠUR (𒀸𒋩)

The doubled š indicates the Assyrian pronunciation
Sumerogram NIN.LÍL (𒊩𒌆𒆤), 'lady of the wind'
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
Consort of Enlil and mother of Nanna/Sîn
Sumerogram NIN.URTA (𒊩𒌆𒅁)
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
God of war, agriculture, and the south wind
Sumerogram AN.ŠAR (𒊚𒊏), 'whole sky'
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
Primordial deity, father of Anu in the Enuma Elish
Sumerogram KI.ŠAR (𒆠𒊏), 'whole earth'
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
Primordial earth goddess, counterpart of Anšar

Akkadian Adad / Sumerian Ishkur
Sumerogram GILGAMESH (𒄑𒂆𒈦)
Standard royal name of the king of Uruk

Sumerogram NIN.ḪUR.SAĜ (𒊩𒌆𒉺𒍇), 'lady of the mountain'
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
Great mother goddess, syncretised with Damkina/Nintur

Monster guardian of the Cedar Forest in the Gilgamesh epic
Sumerogram ÉREŠ.KI.GAL (𒊕𒆠𒃲), 'lady of the great earth'
Prefixed with divine determinative 𒀭
Queen of the underworld

steps: Ugaritic alphabetic cuneiform ʿ-n-t
Initial ʿayin is a voiced pharyngeal fricative
PUNYCODEX uses Egyptological Ain (ꜥ) as the registrable stand-in for ʿayin
Ugaritic ʾ-a-ṯ-r-t; the third sign ṯ = /θ/ > /ʃ/
Full title: rbt ʾaṯrt ym, 'Lady Asherah of the Sea'
The macron over ē marks the long vowel inferred from Hebrew אֲשֵׁרָה
sources: Day, Yahweh and the Gods and Goddesses of Canaan

steps: Ugaritic b-ʿ-l, the West Semitic title 'lord'
Initial ʿayin is rendered with Egyptological Ain (ꜥ) for DNS registrability
As divine name, often paired with Haddu/Hadad, the storm god
Ugaritic ʾ-l, the common Semitic word for 'god' used as the high god's name
The macron over ē marks the long vowel of the nominative case
Hebrew אֵל and Arabic ʾilāh are cognates
sources: Cross, Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic

steps: Phoenician ʾ-š-r-t
Cognate with Ugaritic Asherah and Hebrew ʾăšērâ
The final -u marks the nominative case in older Northwest Semitic
sources: Day, Yahweh and the Gods and Goddesses of Canaan

steps: Phoenician m-w-t, the common Semitic root for 'death'
The macron over ō marks the long vowel inferred from Ugaritic / Hebrew cognates
Personified Death in the Ugaritic Baal Cycle
Phoenician y-m, the Semitic word for 'sea'
The doubled mm in the absolute state produces Yammu
Personified Sea in the Baal Cycle
Phoenician š-p-š, the Northwest Semitic sun-goddess
The macron over ā marks the long vowel of the feminine noun
Ugaritic counterpart Šapšu
sources: Pardee, Ritual and Cult at Ugarit

steps: Phoenician k-t-r, 'skilled one'
The circumflex over ô marks a long vowel resulting from contraction
Ugaritic Kothar-wa-Ḫasīs, the craftsman god
Phoenician d-g-n, the grain god
The macron over ā marks the long vowel inferred from cognates
Worshipped at Ugarit and in the Levant
Phoenician ʾ-š-t-r-t, 'she of the womb'
The planet Venus as goddess; cognate with Mesopotamian Ištar
Final -u marks the older nominative case ending
Phoenician ʾ-š-t-r-t, 'she of the womb'
The planet Venus as goddess; cognate with Mesopotamian Ištar
PUNYCODEX uses the shortened nominative Aštart as the primary form
Mouth sign R (𓂋) + sun-disk alef (𓏤)
The final ꜥ represents a glottal stop or voiced pharyngeal
Egyptian sun-god, later fused with Amun as Amun-Ra
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Throne (ws) + eye (jr) ideogram, conventionally read Wsjr
The exact vocalisation is unknown; Coptic ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲣⲉ supplies a late reflex
God of the underworld and resurrection
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Recumbent jackal (𓃢) as ideogram and determinative
Full phonetic spelling can include 𓇋𓈖𓊪𓅱
God of mummification and guide of the dead
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Falcon on a perch (𓅃), the Horus-falcon logogram
Stands for the sky-god and divine kingship
The initial Ḥ marks a voiceless pharyngeal fricative
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Throne sign (𓊨) + bread (t) + egg determinative (𓆇)
The throne sign is a rebus for the name Isis
Goddess of magic and motherhood
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Ibis (𓅜) + bread sign (𓏏), logogram for the moon-god of writing
Full phonetic spelling 𓆓𓏌𓏏𓆇 is also attested
The initial Ḏ marks a voiced palato-alveolar affricate
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Ogdoad-plume sign (𓁩), the hidden god of Thebes
Phonetic spelling 𓇋𓏠𐎕𓈖 is also used
The name means 'the hidden one'
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Mummified god with enclosed hieroglyph (𓁣), the craftsman-god
Phonetic spelling 𓊪𓏏𓎛 is also attested
Creator god of Memphis
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Lioness head (𓃭) as logogram for the powerful goddess
Full spelling 𓄥𓎡𓏠𓏏𓆇 adds phonetic complements
Warrior aspect of the solar eye
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Cat or cat-headed sign (𓃠) + feminine ending (𓏏)
The name contains bꜣs, 'ointment jar', with the cat determinative
Protective goddess of home and childbirth
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Mansion (ḥwt) containing a falcon (ḥr), 'House of Horus'
Goddess of love, music, and motherhood
Often written with the sistrum as an additional determinative
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Feather (mꜣꜥt) on the head of a seated woman (𓁦)
The feather itself is the logogram for truth/order
Goddess of cosmic order and justice
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Set-animal (𓃫) as logogram and determinative
Phonetic spelling 𓆓𓏏𓐍 is also used
God of chaos, storms, and the desert
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Water-pot hieroglyph (𓇯) as phonogram and logogram
Goddess of the sky, arched over the earth
The vowels are reconstructed from Coptic ⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: White-fronted goose (𓅬) as logogram for the earth-god
The goose is a rebus for Gb 'earth'
Lies beneath Nut, the sky-goddess
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Ostrich feather (𓄑) as logogram for the air-god
The name is connected to šw 'dry, empty'
Separates Nut and Geb
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Crocodile (𓃣) as logogram for the crocodile-god
Full spelling 𓄥𓃀𓎡 adds phonetic complements
God of the Nile and fertility
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Child moon-god with lunar disk (𓁤) as logogram
Full spelling 𓐍𓈖𓇓𓅱 adds phonetic complements
Member of the Theban triad with Amun and Mut
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Ram with horizontal horns (𓃞) as logogram
Full spelling 𓐍𓈖𓀔 adds phonetic complements
Potter-god who shapes humans on his wheel
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Basket (nb) + house (ḥwt) + feminine determinative
'Lady of the mansion', sister of Isis
Protectress of the dead and the sarcophagus
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Jackal on a standard (𓃧), 'opener of the ways'
Full spelling 𓃧𓊪𓅱𓏏𓆇 adds phonetic complements
Guide and scout of the divine procession
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Scarab beetle (𓆣) as logogram for the becoming one
Full spelling 𓐍𓊪𓂋𓇋 adds phonetic complements
Morning form of the sun-god
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian

steps: Water sign (𓈗) as logogram for the primordial waters
Full spelling 𓈖𓈖𓏌 adds phonetic complements
Personification of the pre-creation watery abyss
sources: Faulkner, A Concise Dictionary of Middle Egyptian
